types: AQA's AS papers open each section with one-mark multiple-choice questions, and the A-level papers use them for skills such as reading a graph or choosing a statistical test. Every one here has its answer.
The first question in each A-level section: point-marked, so each developed point earns marks. No evaluation needed, and no levels.

"Analyse the data shown in Figure 1": levels-marked AO3 questions that reward patterns, trends, anomalies and the use of figures from the resource. Describing without manipulating the data stays in Level 1.
Using the figure and your own knowledge (6 and 9 marks)
A-level questions that combine the resource with your own knowledge (AO1 and AO2): the top level needs both, linked.
The 9-mark Assess questions and the 20-mark Evaluate and To what extent essays that end each option. The top level needs a sustained argument, case-study detail and a substantiated conclusion.
Questions that ask you to link two or more parts of the specification, usually the 9-mark question on the AS papers and in the A-level options.
AS Paper 2 Section B: questions on your own fieldwork and on unfamiliar fieldwork data, from sampling and risk to the conclusions you could draw.
Every question where the marks need a calculation: means, ranges, percentages, rates of change and statistical tests.
AS short-answer questions on the content, a resource or a method: precise and quick.
searchHint: e.g. storm hydrograph, longshore drift, tectonics, place
levelsNote: AQA marks the 6-mark questions in two levels (1–3, 4–6), the 9-markers in three (1–3, 4–6, 7–9) and the 20-mark essays in four (1–5, 6–10, 11–15, 16–20). The top level needs detailed knowledge applied to the question, a sustained argument with evidence, and a conclusion that follows from it.
